_note: The parameter catalogue for this corpus: every number a statute did not state, with its unit (the corpus's own units are accepted and scaled by the decoder), the convention its value comes from and its source. It starts empty: the plan decides which parameters exist and proposes each with a provisional value, and the harness enters the proposal here marked `proposed` (run, iteration, node) until the operator reviews it by removing the marker or changing the value; the doctor lists every unreviewed proposal. The operator-authored list this file carried before any law was planned is kept, out of the pipeline's path, under readings/legacy/. Figures the law states are literals on the rule's span, never entries here.

params.name: p.stop_speed_tolerance
params.convention: The sampled-speed threshold at or below which a road user counts as not moving, as stop-sign compliance observation uses it; it bounds the definition's absolute 'complete cessation from movement' against sensor noise and sampling, and is the smallest commitment the word requires.
params.source: ITE and FHWA stop-sign compliance field studies; naturalistic-driving stop classification thresholds

params.name: p.stop_dwell_time
params.convention: The dwell for which the speed must stay at or below the tolerance before a halt counts as a cessation rather than a sampling artefact of a slow roll, as the same compliance observation practice uses it.

params.name: p.slowing_decel
params.convention: The mean deceleration over the approach window that separates a yield-sign slowing from an unchanged approach speed, taken at the lower end of the comfortable-deceleration range so that only an unchanged approach fails it.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book, comfortable deceleration for approach manoeuvres

params.name: p.slowing_window
params.convention: The window behind the observation over which that mean deceleration is measured: the time a vehicle takes to cover the final length of a yield-controlled approach at approach speed.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book, intersection approach practice

params.name: p.approach_sight_distance
params.convention: Intersection sight distance: the length of the priority leg that must be visible from the departure point for a stopped vehicle to clear the crossing, which is what a vehicle approaching at the priority road's design speed covers in that clearing time.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book, intersection sight distance, Case B1 (stop control on the minor road)

params.name: p.conflict_horizon
params.convention: The look-ahead of the constant-velocity conflict prediction the closest-approach primitives run, taken from the time-to-collision band within which surrogate-safety analysis counts an encounter as a conflict; beyond it a prediction from present velocities carries no information.
params.source: FHWA Surrogate Safety Assessment Model (SSAM), time-to-collision threshold

params.name: p.conflict_clearance
params.convention: The separation at the predicted closest approach below which two bodies count as conflicting rather than passing: a passenger-car half-width plus a working margin, applied to centre-to-centre closest approach and read against the measured surface gap.
params.source: FHWA SSAM conflict criteria with standard passenger-car dimensions

params.name: p.immediate_hazard_gap
params.convention: Critical headway: the gap in the priority stream below which a crossing manoeuvre from a stop- or yield-controlled approach is not accepted. A vehicle whose predicted time to closest approach is under it is approaching so closely as to be an immediate hazard.
params.source: Highway Capacity Manual, base critical headway for crossing movements at two-way stop-controlled intersections

params.name: p.induced_decel
params.convention: The deceleration the priority vehicle must not be forced past for precedence to have been granted: the threshold above which braking stops being an ordinary speed adjustment and becomes a response to a vehicle taken in front of it.
params.source: AASHTO Green Book comfortable deceleration, as surrogate-safety practice applies it to induced braking

params.name: p.stop_dwell
params.convention: halt convention: the time a body must stay within the speed tolerance for the halt to be distinguished from a single slow sample at ordinary trace rates; it instantiates the concept's dwell.
params.source: stopped-vehicle detection practice; sampling rates of trajectory datasets.

params.name: p.precedence_window
params.convention: The look-back over which one road user's conduct towards another is read as a granting of precedence: the brake-reaction interval of the receiving driver, the span within which a vehicle that must give way has either stayed clear of the other or forced it to brake. It instantiates the window parameter drv.interaction.precedence_granted leaves to its caller; a shorter span reads the granting off a single sample, a longer one makes the constant-velocity prediction of the whole approach part of the judgement.
params.source: AASHTO, A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets: the brake-reaction time used in the stopping-sight-distance model.

_fields.aggregates: optional operator overrides only: word, classes (ru.* ids or other words). The run derives every aggregate the laws use from the corpus definitions (results/<run>/reading.json, for review); an operator entry here takes precedence over the derived one.
